sanskrit: अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च । नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥
hindiTranslation: यह शरीरी काटा नहीं जा सकता, यह जलाया नहीं जा सकता, यह गीला नहीं किया जा सकता और यह सुखाया भी नहीं जा सकता ।  कारण कि यह नित्य रहनेवाला सबमें परिपूर्ण, अचल, स्थिर स्वभाववाला और अनादि है ॥
englishTranslation: This embodied self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, unmoving, fixed, and timeless.
essence: What you are cannot be harmed by anything that changes.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: The true self cannot be destroyed by any physical force. It is permanent, present everywhere, unmoving, and beyond time.
simpleInsight: What you truly are is untouched by change, so fear loses its grip.
detailedMeaning: Krishna deepens his teaching: the inner being cannot be harmed the way a body can. This verse strengthens the case for acting without grief.
modernRelevance: A man laid off at fifty-five can feel he has been cut down to nothing. Krishna's list says otherwise about the self: it cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried, and it is eternal.
translationLiteral: अच्छेद्यः (uncuttable) / अयम् (this) / अदाह्यः (unburnable) / अयम् (this) / अक्लेद्यः (unwettable) / अशोष्यः (undryable) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / नित्यः (eternal) / सर्वगतः (all-pervading) / स्थाणुः (fixed) / अचलः (unmoving) / अयम् (this) / सनातनः (timeless)
insight: Krishna piles up the words for the self: uncuttable, unburnable, eternal, all-pervading, unmoving and fixed.
